paragraphs.zh: In at least one embodiment, the enol ester of formula (II) can be prepared by reacting NMSBA of formula(III)with 1, 3-cyclohexanedionein presence of N,N'-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent. The solvent may be any solvent in which NMSBA of formula (III) and/or 1,3-cyclohexanedione may be soluble. Examples of solvent include dichloromethane, dichloroethane, dichloropropanes, dichlorobutanes, dichloropentanes,and mixtures thereof. Preferably, the solvent can be dichloromethane. In various embodiments, the disclosed process can produce enol ester of formula (II) in high yields, e.g. at least 65%, with a purity of at least 85%. In another embodiment, the disclosed process can produce solvent recovery of >85%.
paragraphs.en: In at least one embodiment, the enol ester of formula (II) can be prepared by reacting NMSBA of formula(III)with 1, 3-cyclohexanedionein presence of N,N'-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and a solvent. Examples of solvent include dichloromethane, dichloroethane, dichloropropanes, dichlorobutanes, dichloropentanes,and mixtures thereof. Preferably, the solvent can be dichloromethane. drawings.notes: Two labels are printed under the drawing, centred beneath the structure each names: 'Formula IV' under the toluene on the left and 'Formula III' under the benzoic acid on the right. Both are printed without parentheses, whereas the prose beside them writes 'formula (IV)' and 'formula (III)' with parentheses; the label strings are recorded in name exactly as printed under the drawings. Nothing is written below the arrow; reagents_below is empty because that position is genuinely blank, not because it could not be read. The single label above the arrow is one printed string, 'Oxidant / RuO2' with the subscript 2 on the oxygen, and it is recorded as one item because the slash is printed, not inferred. Every stroke in this scheme is broken dotted ink, as the front page warns for a black and white reproduction; the arrow is a degraded solid line with one solid filled arrowhead at the right and is NOT a dashed arrow. Substituent positions were read off vertex geometry, not inferred from the names: the hexagon is drawn with top and bottom vertices, CH3 (left structure) or the carboxyl (right structure) on the top vertex, SO2CH3 on the bottom vertex which is para to it, and NO2 on the upper right vertex which is ortho to the top vertex and meta to SO2CH3. Both SMILES were parsed with rdkit and give C8H9NO4S for Formula IV and C8H7NO6S for Formula III.

drawings.notes: The arrow in this scheme carries NO writing at all, above or below it. Both reagent lists are empty because both positions are genuinely blank on the page, not because anything was unreadable; the prose on this page names reagents for this step and the drawing does not, which is recorded in discrepancies. Two labels are printed under the drawing: 'Formula III' under the benzoic acid on the left and 'Formula II' under the product on the right, again without parentheses where the prose uses them. The 1,3-cyclohexanedione in the middle carries no printed label of any kind, so its name is null even though the prose one line above names 1,3-cyclohexanedione as the second reactant; the identification of the drawing rests on the drawing itself, whose two carbonyls are one carbon apart. The product ring geometry was measured rather than eyeballed, because the benzene ring in this drawing is only about 90 by 100 pixels: vertex centres at 6x magnification put the ester carbonyl attachment and the nitro vertex adjacent, and the SO2CH3 attachment three bonds round from the ester attachment, so nitro is ortho and SO2CH3 is para to the ester as in Formula III. In the cyclohexenone ring the ester oxygen sits on the lower left vertex, a clear double bond runs up the left edge from that vertex to the upper left vertex, and the ketone =O sits on the top vertex, which makes the product the enol ester of 1,3-cyclohexanedione with the oxo group two bonds from the enol oxygen. All strokes are broken dotted ink and the arrow is a degraded solid line with one solid filled arrowhead; it is not dashed. SMILES parsed with rdkit: C6H8O2 for the diketone and C14H13NO7S for Formula II, which is an isomer of mesotrione, consistent with the rearrangement the patent describes elsewhere.
